message.content:
### Building a New PC – Step‑by‑Step Guide

Below is a practical, beginner‑friendly walkthrough.  
Feel free to skip sections you already know, but keep the order for safety and best results.

| # | What to Do | Why It Matters | Tips |
|---|------------|----------------|------|
| **1** | **Plan & Budget** | Know what you’ll use it for (gaming, video editing, office, etc.) | List required specs: CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, PSU, case, cooling. |
| **2** | **Gather Parts** | All components must be compatible. | Use a PC builder tool (e.g., PCPartPicker) to check compatibility. |
| **3** | **Prepare Workspace** | Clean, static‑free area. | Anti‑static wrist strap or work on a non‑conductive mat. |
| **4** | **Open the Case** | Access motherboard, power supply, drives. | Remove side panels; keep screws handy. |
| **5** | **Install the Power Supply (PSU)** | Supplies power to all components. | Align the PSU fan with the case vent, screw in, route cables. |
| **6** | **Mount the Motherboard** | Base for all other components. | Align standoffs, screw in, leave a few screws loose for later. |
| **7** | **Install the CPU** | Central processing unit. | Open the socket latch, align the CPU (triangle marker), gently place, lock latch. |
| **8** | **Apply Thermal Paste & Install CPU Cooler** | Keeps CPU from overheating. | Use a pea‑size amount; spread evenly. Attach cooler, secure. |
| **9** | **Insert RAM Modules** | Memory for multitasking. | Open DIMM slots, align notch, press until clicks. |
| **10** | **Mount Storage Drives (SSD/HDD)** | Data storage. | For M.2 SSDs, slide into slot; for 2.5”/3.5” drives, use drive bays or brackets. |
| **11** | **Install the Graphics Card (GPU)** | Handles rendering for games, video, etc. | Slide into PCI‑e x16 slot, secure with screws, connect power cables. |
| **12** | **Connect Power Cables** | Power all components. | 24‑pin ATX, 8‑pin EPS for CPU, 6/8‑pin PCI‑e for GPU, SATA power for drives. |
| **13** | **Connect Data Cables** | Data transfer between components. | SATA data cables for HDD/SSD, M.2 connectors, USB headers, front panel connectors. |
| **14** | **Attach Case Fans & Front Panel** | Cooling and connectivity. | Connect 3‑pin or 4‑pin fan headers, USB, audio, power button, reset button. |
| **15** | **Cable Management** | Improves airflow, aesthetics, easier future upgrades. | Use zip ties, Velcro straps, route cables behind motherboard tray. |
| **16** | **Double‑Check Connections** | Prevents hardware damage. | Ensure no loose screws, all cables firmly seated. |
| **17** | **Close the Case** | Protect components, finish look. | Screw side panels back on. |
| **18** | **Power On & BIOS Setup** | Verify hardware detection. | Press power button; enter BIOS (usually F2, DEL). Check CPU, RAM, storage, GPU. |
| **19** | **Install Operating System (OS)** | Makes PC usable. | Create bootable USB (Windows, Linux, etc.), boot, install. |
| **20** | **Install Drivers & Updates** | Optimal performance, stability. | Download motherboard chipset, GPU, Wi‑Fi, audio drivers. Run Windows Update or distro updates. |
| **21** | **Test & Benchmark** | Ensure everything works correctly. | Run stress tests (Prime95, 3DMark, CrystalDiskMark). Monitor temperatures. |
| **22** | **Enjoy & Maintain** | Keep system running smoothly. | Clean dust filters, update drivers, monitor temperatures. |

---

#### Quick Checklist

- **CPU** – Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen 5/7/9
- **Motherboard** – Matching socket, chipset, form factor (ATX, mATX, mini‑ITX)
- **RAM** – 16 GB DDR4/DDR5 (minimum 8 GB for basic use)
- **GPU** – NVIDIA RTX 3060/3070/3080 or AMD Radeon RX 6600/6700/6800
- **Storage** – NVMe SSD (250 GB–1 TB) + optional SATA HDD (1 TB+)
- **PSU** – 550 W–750 W 80+ Gold (adjust for GPU power)
- **Case** – ATX mid‑tower with good airflow
- **Cooling** – Stock cooler or aftermarket air/liquid cooler
- **Operating System** – Windows 11/10, Ubuntu, Fedora, etc.

---

#### Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short‑circuit** | Use anti‑static wrist strap; never touch metal contacts while components are powered. |
| **CPU not seated** | Double‑check alignment; ensure latch is fully locked. |
| **GPU not recognized** | Verify power connectors are attached; check BIOS for PCI‑e slot selection. |
| **No POST** | Check power cable connections, PSU switch, and that all cables are firmly seated. |
| **Overheating** | Ensure proper airflow, clean dust filters, use quality thermal paste. |

---

#### Resources

- **PCPartPicker** – Build planner & compatibility checker.  
- **YouTube Channels** – Linus Tech Tips, JayzTwoCents, Paul's Hardware.  
- **Reddit** – r/buildapc for community help.  
- **Manufacturer Manuals** – Always read the motherboard, PSU, and case manuals.

---

### Final Thought

Building a PC is a rewarding project that gives you full control over performance and aesthetics. Take your time, double‑check every connection, and enjoy the process! If you hit a snag, feel free to ask for specific help. Happy building!
